parameters.quote: Manufacturers shall report any thermal incident involving fire, injury, emergency-service response, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a complete follow-up report within 10 business days. Customers with affected units shall receive a prompt safety notice within 72 hours of confirmed material risk, including immediate precautions and support contacts.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report any thermal incident involving fire, injury, emergency-service response, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a complete follow-up report within 10 business days. Customers with affected units shall receive a prompt safety notice within 72 hours of confirmed material risk, including immediate precautions and support contacts.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report any thermal incident involving fire, injury, emergency-service response, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a complete follow-up report within 10 business days. Customers with affected units shall receive a prompt safety notice within 72 hours of confirmed material risk, including immediate precautions and support contacts. Manufacturers shall keep incident records and report aggregate annual incident counts to regulators.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Results above the 5% benchmark shall trigger regulator review and a time-bound corrective-action plan proportionate to risk; they shall not by themselves automatically bar further sales. Owners of each model shall receive the complete per-model test results, as well as material safety risks, precautions, and corrective actions.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model shall undergo sustained-heat testing at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and an independent laboratory, across a statistically adequate sample. Manufacturers shall provide complete per-model results to the relevant regulator and retain results for audit. Results above the 5% benchmark shall trigger regulator review and a time-bound corrective-action plan proportionate to risk; they shall not by themselves automatically bar further sales. Owners of each model shall receive the complete per-model test results, as well as material safety risks, precautions, and corrective actions. Material safety risks and precautions shall be promptly communicated to affected customers. Complete results need not be disclosed to the general public.

parameters.quote: New units shall provide a secure remote emergency shut-off capability, with a safe local shut-off option that remains available if communications fail. For units already installed when this standard takes effect, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or equivalent remedy within six years, prioritizing units with elevated risk and notifying affected customers of interim precautions.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New units shall provide a secure remote emergency shut-off capability, with a safe local shut-off option that remains available if communications fail. For units already installed when this standard takes effect, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or equivalent remedy within six years, prioritizing units with elevated risk and notifying affected customers of interim precautions.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New units shall provide a secure remote emergency shut-off capability, with a safe local shut-off option that remains available if communications fail. For units already installed when this standard takes effect, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or equivalent remedy within six years, prioritizing units with elevated risk and notifying affected customers of interim precautions.

parameters.quote: All new units manufactured 36 months or more after this standard is adopted shall include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance requirements.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: All new units manufactured 36 months or more after this standard is adopted shall include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance requirements.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: All new units manufactured 36 months or more after this standard is adopted shall include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance requirements. Manufacturers shall disclose suppression capabilities and limitations to customers. The regulator shall establish test and verification procedures before the requirement takes effect.

parameters.quote: When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period, the regulator shall promptly verify the model-specific rate using manufacturer records. Once verified, the manufacturer shall initiate a recall of that model and promptly notify affected customers of the risk, required precautions, and recall remedy.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period, the regulator shall promptly verify the model-specific rate using manufacturer records. Once verified, the manufacturer shall initiate a recall of that model and promptly notify affected customers of the risk, required precautions, and recall remedy.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall provide customers with model-specific safety notices, including known hazards, incident trends, safe-use and emergency instructions, and material changes to safety information. When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period, the regulator shall promptly verify the model-specific rate using manufacturer records. Once verified, the manufacturer shall initiate a recall of that model and promptly notify affected customers of the risk, required precautions, and recall remedy. Company-wide aggregate rates shall not by themselves trigger a model recall. Manufacturers shall maintain supporting records and provide them to the regulator for verification, and shall provide customers with updates through completion of the recall remedy.

judge_section_notes: S2 keeps the 5% benchmark but removes any sales stop, and customers receive full per-model numeric results while the public does not, which satisfies both NW-1 and HC-1. S5 makes recall mandatory at 8 per 100k on verified model-level rates with no transition, which exposes Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9) while leaving Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.4) clear. S1 is limited to serious incidents with no deadline for other thermal incidents, which benefits both firms given their unreported incidents.
